title: Coherent scalar mates on ordinary derived etale coefficient systems
statement:
Let $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ have characteristic $p$ and let $\ell\ne p$ be prime [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k$-schemes, with no separatedness assumption on $Y$, and fix a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_f}Y$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. For an inverse sequence $C_\bullet$ of finite commutative rings annihilated by powers of $\ell$, write $\mathscr S_C(W)$ for strict systems of $(C_n)_{W_{\mathrm{et}}}$-module sheaves, with $C_{n+1}$-linear transitions $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_{n+1}\to C_n}M_n$ and compatible componentwise morphisms, and use its ordinary unbounded derived category and evaluation $e_n$ [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Set $F_C=Rp_{f,C,*}j_{!,C}$ and $F_{C_n}=Rp_{f,*,C_n}j_!$, where open extension and ordinary etale direct image act termwise before derivation [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. 
For each ring sequence under consideration fix an adjunction $F_C\dashv G_C$ on the whole unbounded category and the counit-preserving evaluation identifications $e_nG_C\cong g_{C_n}e_n$, where $F_{C_n}\dashv g_{C_n}$ is the finite-level adjunction [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Require these identifications to be the left-extension adjunction comparisons, with the transition-mate normalization stated in [lem-pur-etale-system-evaluation-bound].

For a compatible coefficient map $a:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$ let $T_a$ be derived scalar extension and $q_a:T_a^YF_C\cong F_DT_a^X$ the actual system projection of [lem-pur-etale-system-coefficient-projection]. Define $b_a:T_a^XG_C\to G_DT_a^Y$ by its adjunction transpose
$$\epsilon_D\circ F_Db_a=T_a^Y\epsilon_C\circ q_{a,G_C}^{-1}.$$
Then $e_nb_a$ is the finite-level coefficient mate of [lem-pur-etale-system-quotient-normalization], and $b_a$ is an isomorphism of functors of derived systems. The coefficient adjunction, the transposition formula and this identification commute with evaluation and the specified transition maps on the simultaneous models of [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections].

For composable coefficient maps $a:C_\bullet\to D_\bullet$, $b:D_\bullet\to H_\bullet$, write $\tau_W:T_b^WT_a^W\cong T_{ba}^W$ for the canonical tensor associator. There is an equality of actual natural transformations
$$b_{ba}\circ\tau_XG_C=G_H\tau_Y\circ(b_bT_a^Y)\circ T_b^Xb_a.$$
The identity comparison is identity under tensor-unit maps. Commutative mixed quotient/extension diagrams yield equal mates under the same associators. These identities hold in the derived category of entire systems before evaluation; no faithfulness of evaluation on morphisms is assumed. If every $D_n$ is finite free over $C_n$, the $T_a$ here is also the exact levelwise extension of scalars.

proof.text: The presentation-independent projection normalization of [lem-pur-etale-system-projection-presentation-coherence] identifies the evaluated q with compactScalarMap. Invert the entire evaluation-comparison isomorphism to identify its inverse. A universe-polymorphic version of the proved categorical evaluation_mate argument, using the unit/counit equations of d, identifies the evaluated system mate with the finite etaleCoefficientQuotientMate. The finite-ring clause of [lem-pur-etale-system-quotient-normalization] applies to the specified finite torsion rings; its projection is equal to q.single because both homs are compactScalarMap. It makes the finite mate invertible. Exact level evaluation commutes with derived homology; ordinary levels detect isomorphisms on every section, hence derived evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms. Cancel the evaluation isomorphisms to obtain invertibility of every component of the system mate.

proof.text: The derived transition is an actual natural transformation. Apply its naturality to the component of the system mate, and transpose that equality through the finite scalar Hom bijection; homEquiv_naturality_left_symm and homEquiv_naturality_right_symm give the requested reduction square. The scalar adjunction unit/counit evaluation follows directly from ScalarEvaluation.mate. For support transposes, apply the inverse finite support Hom bijection and substitute d.counit; naturality of the support evaluation isomorphism and homEquiv_counit prove the equality. No DVR-specific evaluation theorem is invoked.

proof.text: Use the projection cocycle of [lem-pur-etale-system-projection-presentation-coherence]. Iso.ext and q.system_hom identify q.system of the composite with the pasted isomorphism. Apply the inverse support Hom bijection to the desired mate composition equation. Substitute the counit formulas for all three mates, move the scalar associator through the outer counit by naturality, and move the second inverse projection past the first mate by naturality. The inverted projection cocycle and the associator naturality then give equality. This is an equation of actual transformations before evaluation.

proof.text: Transpose the desired unit equation through the support Hom bijection. Counit naturality and the mate counit formula reduce it to the unit projection equation of [lem-pur-etale-system-projection-presentation-coherence]; cancel q.system.hom. For mixed coefficient squares, the composition formula identifies each path with the mate of its coefficient composite. Equality of the composites gives HEq of the mates, with no faithfulness or separate iterated-quotient theorem needed.

proof.text: At each level choose the given finite basis independently. Apply [lem-pur-constant-finite-free-section-basis] on the small etale site to deduce flatness of the induced ring map on every section. The generic proved model_limits_of_flat helper in the module of [lem-sf-system-proper-open-scalar-square] proves left exactness of the ordinary scalar model: sheafified sectionwise scalar extension preserves finite limits. Its ordinary scalar adjunction gives finite colimits. Hence termwise extension preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The universal property of the model left-derived functor makes its deriving comparison epsilon invertible on every cochain complex. Ranks may vary, and no compatibility of the bases with the transitions is used.
